subject: Anchored per-token ceiling & flexible commit plan
messages:
From: Michael Zhou <mzhou@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal framing: per-token ceiling request + flexible commit option

Hi Rachel —

We're starting internal planning for our May renewal and wanted to surface two asks before we get into contract redlines:

1) Per-token ceiling: given our unpredictable seasonal spikes, we'd like a hard per-token ceiling (an upper per-token price) that prevents surprise unit-price increases between terms. We understand the tiered discounts but want an anchored cap.

2) Flexible commit: Acme is open to a multi-tier commit (e.g., base commit + optional buffer) but need a clear true-up mechanism and an uplift limit year-over-year. We are sensitive to >20% renewal uplifts.

Can Redwood share an example structure (math + worked example) and any guardrails you can offer for renewal uplift? We'll need this to brief procurement.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Zhou
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

Michael — thanks for laying this out. Good timing; we're finalizing renewals for a few customers with similar asks. High-level thoughts: 

- We can offer an "anchored per-token ceiling" as a contract term that limits the maximum per-token price for the next 12 months. That ceiling would apply across the hosted API rates in the proposal.
- For flexibility, a two-tier commit (Base Commit + Optional Buffer) works well: base priced at a deeper discount, buffer at a smaller discount, with a quarterly true-up.
- We are comfortable putting an annual renewal uplift guardrail in the SOW/Order Form — common ask is 10–25% depending on prior usage growth. We can propose a 15% uplift cap as a starting point.

Marissa and Karthik — can you draft two concrete options (A/B) with worked examples (monthly spend and per-token math) and a recommended default? Please attach any proposal PDFs.

Michael — we'll aim to have draft options by EOD Thursday so procurement can review next week. If you have internal thresholds (max uplift, minimum committed units) share them and we'll bake into the examples.

Best,
Rachel

Team — attaching two options (PDF + worked spreadsheet) per Rachel's ask. Summary below so we can sync quickly with Acme: 

Option A — Conservative Anchor
- Base commit: 120M tokens/year at $0.0016/token
- Buffer: up to +30% buffer billed at $0.0019/token
- Per-token ceiling: $0.0022/token (hard cap)
- Renewal uplift cap: 15% year-over-year on list-equivalent spend (applies at amendment)
- Quarterly true-up with pro-rated adjustments

Option B — Growth-Oriented
- Base commit: 80M tokens/year at $0.0014/token
- Buffer: +50% buffer at $0.00185/token
- Per-token ceiling: $0.0025/token
- Renewal uplift cap: 20%
- True-up monthly for buffer, quarterly for base commit shifts

Worked examples in Commit-Tiers-Worked-Example.xlsx show spend math and how uplifts would apply in 3 scenarios (flat, +25% growth, +80% spike). My recommendation is Option A given Acme's ask for a capped ceiling and predictable per-token exposure.

Attachments: Redwood-Proposal-v2.pdf; Commit-Tiers-Worked-Example.xlsx

Marissa Cole

Rachel/Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. A few clarifying questions from procurement and finance: 

1) How is the uplift cap calculated when most of our spend is variable (buffer usage)? Is the cap applied to list-equivalent spend or to the base-commit tier only?
2) In Option A, if we hit +80% spike in month 6 and use buffer extensively, will the per-token ceiling protect us retroactively for that month or only prospectively after true-up?
3) Are there standard language examples you can share for the SOW: a) per-token ceiling clause, b) renewal uplift cap clause, and c) true-up timing?

Procurement would like to model an example where our total token consumption grows 30% YoY — please include that in the worked example.

Regards,
Michael

Subject: Re: Renewal framing: per-token ceiling request + flexible commit option

Michael — answers below and next steps: 

1) Uplift cap basis: We apply the uplift cap to the list-equivalent spend (the notional spend if all usage were billed at the base list rates) at renewal. That prevents large effective price increases driven by a shift in usage mix. We'll show the formula in the spreadsheet.

2) Per-token ceiling applicability: The ceiling is a contractual cap on the per-token rate for the term. It will cap what you pay for buffer months retroactively once invoices are reconciled in the quarterly true-up (i.e., you won't owe more than the ceiling for tokens consumed during the period). The true-up will reflect the ceiling.

3) Standard clause language: see attached proposal PDF (section 4.2) and the sample SOW language below — we'll ask legal to prepare final wording for the Order Form: 

  - Per-token ceiling: "Seller guarantees that the per-token price charged for Hosted API calls will not exceed $X.XX per token for the Term of the Agreement."
  - Renewal uplift cap: "Notwithstanding other pricing provisions, any increase in list-equivalent spend upon renewal shall not exceed 15% relative to the immediately preceding contract year, absent mutual written agreement."
  - True-up timing: "Quarterly reconciliation within 45 days of quarter close; invoices adjusted pro-rata with any overpayment credited on the next invoice."

Next steps: Marissa/Karthik — please convert Option A into redline-ready language for the Order Form (include the ceiling value and the 15% uplift cap) and share a redline draft to Acme's procurement and our Legal by EOD Monday. Michael — if procurement has a counter threshold (e.g., 10% cap), flag it now so we can prepare both variants.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this smoothly.

Rachel Kim
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
